does: Makes an effect entity from an effect resource found by the effect's name and starts it: parameters are the manager, the reference to fill, the name, the level's entity, the scene, a position, a rotation and a scale. The name is turned into a resource id through the map at +0x50 of the global resource manager; a name that is not in it, a resource id included, makes nothing.

evidence.says: It looks the name up with code:unplaced::FindEffectResourceByName, creates the entity with code:unplaced::CreateEffectFromResource and, when the reference is valid, queues the play order with code:unplaced::QueueEffectOrder; the Toolkit exports ls::EffectsManager::PlayEffect(FixedString const&, EntityHandle, Scene*, Vector3f const&, Quaternionf const&, float) with the same eight parameters.

Called on the client with the name VFX_Cinematic_Orin_Teleportation_01, a level's scene and a place, it answers an entity with Effect, Visual, Transform at the place and Level, whose flags say Playing within a second and Stopped when the five seconds effect is over; with the effect's resource id it answers an invalid reference.
GameEngine.dll exports four overloads of this name; which of them this function is is not settled
the macOS build's symbols hold two overloads of this name; it is tied to this function by the job its read shows
